title: If address is a smart contract that can't handle ERC721 tokens they will be stuck after a whitelisted mint
summary: ## Proof of Concept  The `mintPublic` method has a check that allows only EOAs to call it ```solidity if (tx.origin != msg.sender) revert ContractsNotAllowed(); ``` but it is missing in the whitelisted mint methods (`mintArcanaList`, `mintAspirantList`, `mintAllianceList`). This means that if the address that is whitelisted is a contract and it calls those functions but it can't handle ERC721 tokens correctly, they will be stuck.
